role: Independently known subsurface geometry at Giza, for comparison with radar-derived volumes
coordinate_convention: Local metres relative to each monument's base centre: x east, y north, z up from the base platform. Not derived from radar.
caution: Simplified rectilinear models built from published survey dimensions. They are reference geometry, accurate to roughly a metre in size and placement, not engineering drawings or georeferenced masks.

features.name: King's Chamber
features.note: Granite chamber on the pyramid axis, floor about 43 m above the base.

features.name: Queen's Chamber
features.note: On the pyramid axis, corbelled roof.

features.name: Grand Gallery
features.note: Corbelled ascending gallery, 46.7 m along its slope.

features.name: Descending Passage
features.note: Runs from the north entrance down into the bedrock.

features.name: Subterranean Chamber
features.note: Unfinished, cut into bedrock roughly 30 m below the base platform.

features.name: ScanPyramids Big Void
features.note: Detected by muon tomography above the Grand Gallery. Length at least 30 m; cross-section and exact position are not tightly constrained.

features.name: North Face Corridor
features.note: Corridor behind the chevrons on the north face, confirmed by muon imaging and endoscopy.

features.name: Belzoni's Chamber
features.note: Burial chamber cut partly into bedrock at base level, granite sarcophagus in the floor.

features.name: Lower Chamber
features.note: Subsidiary chamber on the lower descending passage.

features.name: Lower Descending Passage
features.note: Begins outside the pyramid on the north side and descends into the bedrock.

references: Petrie, The Pyramids and Temples of Gizeh (1883)
Maragioglio & Rinaldi, L'Architettura delle Piramidi Menfite IV-V
Morishima et al., Discovery of a big void in Khufu's Pyramid, Nature 552, 386 (2017)
Procureur et al., Precise characterization of a corridor-shaped structure in Khufu's Pyramid, Nature Communications 14, 1144 (2023)
